svg.text: Fig 6b - Collision Engine (1/3): Bullet-Wall Scan (one shared maze-RAM lookup, 8 bullets in 8 clocks)
A scan counter time-shares ONE maze-RAM read port across the 8 bullet slots. tile_addr is registered and BRAM read takes 1 clk, so scan index and act are delayed 2 clocks to match.
free-running 0..7; scan_q = bullet index being tested
Every box labelled scan_q[2:0] is the SAME net (output of the scan counter): it selects all four 8:1 muxes
and feeds the delay register at the right. Boxes labelled bN_* are the Fig 5 register outputs.
tile code: 0 floor 1 wall 2 breakable wall 3 unused
2 FFs each: tile_addr register + BRAM read latency,
so scan_d / act_d line up with the tile data
wall_set[i] = wall_hit_now & (scan_d == i) (8 bit-sliced AND gates)
-> sets sticky WALL_HIT_MASK[i] in Fig 6d. Sweep = 8 clocks (+2 latency) = 200 ns @ 50 MHz,
far below one 16.7 ms video frame, so every bullet is checked many times per frame.
The test point is the bullet CENTRE; bounce/lifetime logic itself runs in C.
